writing.label: Written by Prince — not Sinéad O’Connor
trail: The song is credited to Prince, under his own name, on every release. He wrote it in 1984.

Because Sinéad O’Connor’s 1990 recording is so raw and personal — and because it, not Prince’s, is the version the world knows — the writing is widely assumed to be hers. It isn’t: she performed it, and made it famous, but Prince wrote every word and note.

This is the same song’s second story: Prince’s side project The Family recorded it first in 1985 (see above), and O’Connor’s is the cover that eclipsed it. One song, two things the public gets wrong — who recorded it first, and who wrote it.

answer.label: Not a Sinéad O’Connor original — a 1985 album cut by The Family
answer.originalArtistDates: Prince side project · Paisley Park Records, 1985
answer.sourceLine: It is one of the great cover-eclipses in pop: almost everyone takes ‘Nothing Compares 2 U’ for a Sinéad O’Connor original, but her 1990 version is a cover. The song was written by Prince and first recorded by his Paisley Park side project The Family in 1985 — a track on their only album that was never released as a single. O’Connor picked it up five years later and took it to No. 1 worldwide.

original.charted: Did not chart; the album itself made little commercial impact
original.cover: Sinéad O’Connor — January 1990, from I Do Not Want What I Haven’t Got, produced with Nellee Hooper and Chris Birkett. UK and US No. 1 (four weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100) and named the world’s No. 1 single of 1990.

docMeta.dd: August 1985 (Paisley Park) — album track, no single, did not chart

trail: The song was written by Prince and first recorded by The Family, one of the first acts on his Paisley Park label, for their self-titled 1985 album — the one song on it he kept under his own name rather than crediting to the band Wikipedia ↗.
The Family’s version was never released as a single and ‘received little recognition’; the band dissolved after one album. That left the composition all but unheard until Sinéad O’Connor recorded it.

O’Connor’s 1990 cover, produced with Nellee Hooper, reached No. 1 in both the UK and the US and was named the world’s top single of the year — so definitive that the 1985 original dropped out of public memory almost entirely. Prince did not release his own version until later: a 1993 live duet, and his original 1984 demo, unheard until 2018 the song history ↗.

authors.name: The Family
authors.heading: About The Family
authors.bio: The Family were one of the first acts signed to Prince’s Paisley Park label, formed in 1984 around St. Paul Peterson and Susannah Melvoin. Their only album, released in 1985, carried the first recording of ‘Nothing Compares 2 U’ — buried as an album track, never a single. The band dissolved almost immediately and later reformed as fDeluxe; it is a quiet irony of pop history that they cut one of the era’s most famous ballads first, and almost nobody knows it.

authors.name: Sinéad O’Connor
authors.heading: Why it gets pinned on Sinéad O’Connor
authors.bio: Sinéad O’Connor (1966–2023) released her cover of ‘Nothing Compares 2 U’ in 1990, and it became so definitive — a global No. 1, her signature song — that it eclipsed the original completely. Her version is genuinely hers and genuinely great; the only error is chronological, the assumption that a 1990 No. 1 must be where the song began. It began in 1985, on an album track that sank.

authors.name: Prince
authors.heading: About Prince
authors.bio: Prince (1958–2016) wrote ‘Nothing Compares 2 U’ and handed it to The Family, keeping his own name on it rather than crediting the band. He is the third figure the song’s fame obscures: not the singer who made it famous, not the band who recorded it first, but the author whose demo of it went unheard until 2018. Performer fame and authorship are different things, and here they belong to different people.

misattribution.heading: The attribution problem
misattribution.intro: This is the cleanest kind of music misattribution: nothing about Sinéad O’Connor’s record is wrong or fake. The only error is believing she originated it — a 1990 cover mistaken for the source.

items.why: O’Connor’s 1990 version is a cover. The song was recorded five years earlier, in 1985, by The Family the history ↗.
Released as an album track and never as a single, it made little impact — which is exactly why the cover could eclipse it so completely. There was no famous original standing in the way.

Prince wrote the song; he is neither the singer who made it a hit nor a member of the band who first recorded it. Authorship and performance are different things, and here they belong to different people.

misattribution.truthLine: Written by Prince, first recorded by The Family in 1985, and made famous — but not originated — by Sinéad O’Connor in 1990 the record ↗.

context.heading: Why the cover ate the original
lead: A cover eclipses its original most completely when the original never had its moment. The Family’s ‘Nothing Compares 2 U’ was a buried album track that vanished when the band dissolved; there was no hit record occupying the public’s memory of the song, so when Sinéad O’Connor’s version arrived it simply became the version, with nothing to displace.

The extra twist here is the writer. Prince, one of the most famous musicians alive, wrote it and gave it away — then held his own recordings back for decades. So the song’s three creators arrived in reverse order of fame: the buried original first, the global hit second, and the author’s own version last of all.
detailsBody: Prince writes the song and demos it, 1984.
The Family record it, 1985; released as an album track, no single, no chart.
The band dissolves; the song goes all but unheard.
Sinéad O’Connor covers it, January 1990 → UK & US No. 1, world’s top single of the year.
Prince releases his own versions later: a 1993 live duet, and his 1984 demo, unheard until 2018.
